hints: Focus on what each unit is really asking for, moles in one case and mass in the other, so you will need the molar mass of glucose to link them.
Start by working out the $M_r$ of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6$ and then use mass = moles x $M_r$ to turn 18.5 mmol into mg.
Remember you are changing both the mass unit and the volume unit, so finish by scaling from per litre to per decilitre (0.1 litre).
walkthrough:
**Find the molar mass of glucose**

Glucose links moles to grams, so we need its $M_r$ first. Add up the atoms carefully.

$$M_r(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6) = (6 \times 12) + (12 \times 1) + (6 \times 16) = 72 + 12 + 96 = 180$$
So 1 mol of glucose = 180 g.

**Convert mmol per litre to mg per litre**

Change millimoles to moles, then to mass. 18.5 mmol is $18.5 \times 10^{-3}$ mol.

$$\text{mass per litre} = 18.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 180 = 3.33 \text{ g/l}$$
Now change grams to milligrams by multiplying by 1000.

$$3.33 \text{ g/l} = 3330 \text{ mg/l}$$

**Convert per litre to per decilitre**

A decilitre is much smaller than a litre. Since $1 \text{ l} = 10 \text{ dl}$, the same mass spread over 10 times more volume units means divide by 10.

$$\frac{3330 \text{ mg}}{10 \text{ dl}} = 333 \text{ mg/dl}$$
That matches the health problem level in the new units.

options.A: Too small by a factor of 10. This happens if you divide by 10 twice, for example converting litres to decilitres correctly but also slipping a decimal when changing g to mg or mmol to mol.
options.B: Close to 180, which is the $M_r$ of glucose. This suggests stopping at the molar mass step or mixing up the scaling, without correctly multiplying 18.5 mmol by 180 mg per mmol and then adjusting for volume.
options.C: Correct. 18.5 mmol/l gives $18.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 180 = 3.33$ g/l = 3330 mg/l, and dividing by 10 for 0.1 dm3 gives 333 mg/dl.
options.D: Exactly 10 times too big. This is the value in mg/l (3330 mg/l). The trap is forgetting that 1 dl = 0.1 l, so you must divide by 10 to go from per litre to per decilitre.
